// AUTO-GENERATED by puerto. Edit puerto.toml, then run `puerto generate bootstrap`.
use std::sync::Arc;

use business::application::product::create_product::CreateProductUseCaseImpl;
use business::application::product::delete_product::DeleteProductUseCaseImpl;
use business::application::product::get_product::GetProductUseCaseImpl;
use business::application::product::list_products::ListProductsUseCaseImpl;
use business::application::product::update_product::UpdateProductUseCaseImpl;

use business::domain::product::repository::ProductRepositoryTrait;
use business::domain::product::unit_of_work::ProductUnitOfWorkFactory;
use infrastructure::product::repository::PgProductRepository;
use infrastructure::product::unit_of_work::PgProductUnitOfWorkFactory;

use poem::Endpoint;
use poem_openapi::OpenApiService;

use crate::api::product::routes::ProductApi;

/// The routes, wired. An error is what stopped the startup: `main` prints it and exits 1.
pub async fn build_app(config: puerto_web::Config) -> Result<impl Endpoint, String> {
    let database_url = std::env::var("DATABASE_URL").map_err(|_| {
        "DATABASE_URL is not set — set it in .env (.env.example has one)".to_string()
    })?;
    let pool = infrastructure::db::create_postgres_pool(&database_url)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| format!("{e} — is the database up? `make docker-compose/up`"))?;
    infrastructure::db::run_migrations(&pool, &infrastructure::db::MIGRATOR)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

    let product_repo: Arc<dyn ProductRepositoryTrait> =
        Arc::new(PgProductRepository::new(pool.clone()));
    let product_uow: Arc<dyn ProductUnitOfWorkFactory> =
        Arc::new(PgProductUnitOfWorkFactory::new(pool.clone()));
    let create_product = Arc::new(CreateProductUseCaseImpl {
        uow_factory: Arc::clone(&product_uow),
    });
    let get_product = Arc::new(GetProductUseCaseImpl {
        repository: Arc::clone(&product_repo),
    });
    let list_products = Arc::new(ListProductsUseCaseImpl {
        repository: Arc::clone(&product_repo),
    });
    let update_product = Arc::new(UpdateProductUseCaseImpl {
        repository: Arc::clone(&product_repo),
        uow_factory: Arc::clone(&product_uow),
    });
    let delete_product = Arc::new(DeleteProductUseCaseImpl {
        repository: Arc::clone(&product_repo),
        uow_factory: Arc::clone(&product_uow),
    });
    let product_api = ProductApi {
        create_product,
        get_product,
        list_products,
        update_product,
        delete_product,
    };

    let ready = puerto_web::health::probe(move || {
        let pool = pool.clone();
        async move { infrastructure::db::ping(&pool).await }
    });

    // `app.rs` is the project's own: middleware and routes added there wrap everything here.
    Ok(crate::app::configure(puerto_web::routes(
        openapi_service(product_api),
        &config,
        ready,
    )))
}

/// The API service, built in one place: whatever else reads its spec (the export test of a project
/// with `web/`) sees the API the server answers.
fn openapi_service<T: poem_openapi::OpenApi>(api: T) -> OpenApiService<T, ()> {
    OpenApiService::new(api, env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME"), env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"))
}
